title: A Confession for the Parish
premise: When the coffin of Harriet Voss, founder of the river town of Calloway's Bend, is found empty during a cemetery relocation, night-shift taxi dispatcher Wendell Okonkwo realizes she has been ferrying the town's secrets for two decades without ever reading them. A cryptic ledger hidden in the taxi company's old fare books—kept by her late mentor, dispatcher Ezra Finch—points to the truth: Voss never died; she vanished, and five prominent families helped bury the lie. As Wendell decodes entries tied to specific fares and addresses, she discovers her own mother was one of the conspirators, forcing her to choose between protecting the found family of dispatchers who raised her and exposing the truth before the town toasts Voss at the centennial anniversary dinner. At the dinner, Wendell reads the ledger aloud; the town fractures, but an elderly woman in the back row—Harriet herself, living quietly under another name—stands and confirms everything, choosing truth over myth.
about_author: Orsen Nakamura is a former small-town radio operator who spent a decade collecting the oral histories of disappearing communities. He writes mysteries about the quiet violence of what towns agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The Empty Glass Case
chapters.summary: Wendell Okonkwo, working the graveyard shift at Calloway Taxi, hears on the police scanner that Harriet Voss's coffin has been opened—and it's empty. POV Wendell. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the sense that the night shift always knows first.

chapters.title: Fares and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wendell sorts through Ezra Finch's inherited fare ledgers while the town buzzes with theories. She notices odd marginal codes beside certain 1998 fares. POV Wendell. Beat: grief for Ezra entwining with curiosity; the ledger feels like a message left for her specifically.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Wendell is strong-armed into driving committee members—Mayor Dellacroce, banker Ruth Pell—to planning meetings for the centennial dinner honoring Voss. Their nervousness registers. POV Wendell. Beat: wry detachment cracking as she clocks who flinches at the word 'exhumed.'

chapters.title: Code of the Night Shift
chapters.summary: Deciphering Ezra's shorthand, Wendell finds repeated runs to the old Voss estate after Voss's supposed death. POV Wendell with flashback to young Wendell learning dispatch from Ezra. Beat: mentor's posthumous voice guiding her; thrill of competence.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Pell
chapters.summary: Ruth Pell hires Wendell's cab for a tense midnight ride to the county records office, then asks her to forget the trip. POV Wendell. Beat: loyalty tested early—the first explicit request to un-see something.

chapters.title: What the Cemetery Knows
chapters.summary: Wendell interviews the gravedigger, Ambrose Teal, who dug the original grave and swears he lowered a full coffin. Someone else filled it. POV Wendell. Beat: dread deepening; the lie was operational, requiring many hands.

chapters.title: Ezra's Last Entry
chapters.summary: In a locked drawer, Wendell finds Ezra's final ledger page: 'She's still taking fares. Ask the lighthouse road.' That night, a cab request comes from the abandoned keeper's cottage. POV Wendell. Beat: spine-chill wonder; the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Lighthouse Road
chapters.summary: Wendell drives out alone and finds fresh footprints, a stocked pantry, and a woman's coat in a style twenty years out of fashion. POV Wendell. Beat: awe and fear braided together—she is close to someone who wants to stay dead.

chapters.title: The Five Families
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing coded fares, Wendell maps five households tied to the cover-up: Dellacroce, Pell, Okafor, Lindqvist, and—her stomach drops—Okonkwo. POV Wendell. Beat: betrayal; the conspiracy includes her own bloodline.

chapters.title: Mother's Alibi
chapters.summary: Wendell confronts her mother, Adaeze, who admits driving a hooded passenger out of town the night Voss 'died'—but claims she was protecting Wendell, not Voss. POV Wendell. Beat: fury and tenderness colliding; family love as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: Dispatch Log, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the taxi office and steals the 1998 ledger. Only three people had keys. POV Wendell. Beat: paranoia; the found family of dispatchers suddenly suspect.

chapters.title: Junior Partner
chapters.summary: Young dispatcher Milo Reyes confesses he copied pages for Mayor Dellacroce to protect his sick sister's job. Wendell chooses to shield him. POV Wendell. Beat: found-family loyalty crystallizing—she protects her own even now.

chapters.title: The Widow's Version
chapters.summary: Wendell tracks down Voss's former housekeeper, Ida Lindqvist, who reveals Voss was dying of cancer and staged her death to escape being canonized into a myth she despised. POV Wendell. Beat: moral vertigo—the empty coffin was mercy, maybe.

chapters.title: Okafor's Warning
chapters.summary: Councilman Okafor offers Wendell money and a promotion to drop it, hinting that 'people who loved you arranged things you shouldn't undo.' POV Wendell. Beat: temptation and insult; the price of silence made concrete.

chapters.title: Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Milo recovers his photocopies; combined with Ezra's codes, they reveal a final destination: the Voss estate's caretaker cottage, fares continuing until eighteen months ago. POV Wendell. Beat: hope sharpening into resolve—Voss may still be alive.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Town descends into festival chaos; Wendell works triple shifts ferrying dignitaries while deciding whether to speak. Ruth Pell suffers a stroke after trying to confess to her. POV Wendell. Beat: ticking clock made flesh; guilt over almost-heard truths.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the centennial dinner, the mayor unveils a statue of Voss. Wendell stands with the ledger as five hundred glasses rise. POV Wendell. Beat: terror and clarity; the moment before speaking.

chapters.title: A Confession for the Parish
chapters.summary: Wendell reads the ledger aloud—every coded fare, every conspirator—including her mother's name. The room detonates; the mayor lunges for the book; Milo records everything. POV Wendell. Beat: catharsis through exposure; no going back.

chapters.title: The Woman in Row Nine
chapters.summary: An old woman rises: Harriet Voss, alive, frail, furious at being made a saint. She confirms the staging and forgives no one, least of all the town that needed her dead to be perfect. POV Wendell. Beat: shock resolving into grim vindication.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Resignations, indictments, and a town splitting into those who thank Wendell and those who spit. Her mother stops speaking to her; Ambrose Teal shakes her hand. POV Wendell. Beat: cost accounting—truth bought at the price of belonging.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Hands
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wendell trains Milo as lead dispatcher, passing on Ezra's codes openly this time. The taxi company becomes the town's honest archive. POV Wendell. Beat: quiet repair; legacy reclaimed rather than inherited.

chapters.title: One Last Fare
chapters.summary: A cab request comes from Lighthouse Road. Wendell drives out herself; Voss wants a ride to the cemetery to see the grave that held her name. They talk like two women who kept secrets. POV Wendell. Beat: peace earned, not given; the door left open for memory to be rewritten honestly.
